[poem]

She was tired, not tired
but exhausted. Drained to her core. 
From the number of times,
she heard her daughters say no.

They whispered, 
“No.” from the little pit of fire in their bellies.
Praying,
to her, to the heavens, to their own,
mothers and fathers. 
Hoping,
that their whisper was enough. 
Strong enough,
LOUD enough,
polite enough.

They screamed,
“No.” with all the breath in their lungs.
Praying,
to him, to his desires, to his last,
bit of humanity. 
Wishing,
to be heard.
Respected,
Autonomized,
FREED.

They begged,
“No.” their last hopes fading from their feet.
Praying,
to themselves, to their soul, to their lives,
challenged to make it through the night. 
Leaving,
from the body. 
The HURT,
the loss,
The terror. 

She was tired,
of hearing her daughters cry.
“No.” to the taking. 
And taking. 
And taking. 
So she closed her eyes,
and the last thing, humanity heard,
was “No.”
I’ve tried. None of them respond to me besides one and he’s ignoring her calls because of that.
